Kostyantynivka is a flashpoint, with regular Russian assault groups engaging in small-arms fire, though it remains under Ukrainian control. Russian forces are attempting to bypass Kostyantynivka via Druzhkivka to create an encirclement. The Siverskyi Lyman area and the Lyman–Yampil axis have become strategically critical: the loss of the Serebrianskyi forest has opened a corridor for advances toward Lyman and Yampil, and capturing Siversk or outflanking Lyman could enable a direct route to Sloviansk, further reducing Ukraine’s operational depth. Druzhkivka, Dobropillya, Kramatorsk, and Sloviansk remain under Ukrainian control but endure daily strikes. Civilian evacuations continue amid relentless attacks. Experts note Russia’s strategy remains hybrid, combining battlefield pressure with information campaigns targeting Ukraine, Europe, and the United States. The outcome of fighting in Lyman, Siversk, Kostyantynivka, and the Pokrovsk–Myrnohrad sector will determine the future of Ukrainian defenses in Sloviansk and Kramatorsk.

articles.title: Kostyantyn Barabanov, a Soldier from Kyiv Oblast, Dies in Donbas Shelling; Multiple Ukrainian Soldiers Killed in Combat
articles.summary: On December 8, 2022, Ukrainian soldier Kostyantyn Barabanov from Lubianka, Kyiv Oblast, died as a result of a hostile shelling on the Donbas front. He was 43 years old and a volunteer mobilized in April 2022. Barabanov, a welder and a man who enjoyed driving and managing a farm, was killed by a Russian shell in a territory occupied by Russian forces at the time, making repatriation impossible for years. His wife, Kateryna, and son, Illia, remain as his surviving family. Bucha city head Anatoliy Fedoruk shared the news in his Telegram channel, stating, 'On the shield, Kostyantyn Barabanov returns home. The hero died on December 8, 2022, on the Donbas front from a hostile shell. That battlefield was occupied by Russians, so bringing Kostyantyn home was impossible for a long time.' Additionally, on June 30, 2024, another soldier from Obukhiv Raion, Kyiv Oblast, Artem Gutsol, a combat medic, died during a combat mission. On July 19, 2024, Oleh Borovik, a soldier from Boyarka, Kyiv Oblast, also died during a combat operation on the Pokrovsk direction. All three soldiers died defending Ukraine’s independence and territorial integrity.
